A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MPR-GUI-Bench and GUI-XLI. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching material relocated or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original multilingual benchmark evaluations, GUI-XLI intervention experiments, ablations, and annotation and translation validation results.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark and intervention results and adds GUI-agent evaluations, generator-source comparisons, correlation analyses, and multilingual annotation statistics.

M1.justification: The specified retrieval key in Eq. 3 changes from the hidden state of question, reasoning chain, and answer in v1 to the question-and-image state in v2. This is a bounded revision to memory retrieval; difference-vector construction, cosine retrieval, averaging, and normalized inference-time intervention remain.

E1.justification: Both retain the 12,936-sample benchmark covering six languages, eight dimensions, 39 scenarios, and six mobile device models across iOS and Android. Recasting RI/SI as end-to-end reasoning does not introduce interactive evaluation. The new generator-source comparison uses the existing GUI task dimensions.

E2.justification: v2 adds UI-TARS-7B-DPO, AgentCPM-GUI-8B, and Show-UI-2B to the benchmark comparison, substantially expanding specialized GUI-agent coverage. MiniCPM-o 2.6, Keye-VL-7B, and CogAgent-9B are retained in Table 21, rather than removed. GPT-4o also becomes an evaluated comparator in the new generator-bias study.

E3.justification: v2 adds a controlled evaluation of GPT-4o-generated versus Gemini-2.5-Pro-generated questions and a correlation-based validation design. The principal exact-match evaluation, FPR-ACC weights, and two-stage layer/strength search remain. Newly supplied intervention settings document existing experiments rather than establish changed budgets or reruns.

E4.justification: v2 adds substantial benchmark-validation analyses: generator-dependence testing in Appendix A.6 and correlations between RI/SI and FPR-ACC in Table 3. It also adds RI/SI examples and a before/after GUI-XLI reasoning case. The earlier t-SNE analysis, hyperparameter study, and six basic-dimension case collections are retained.

E5.justification: v2 supplements Fleiss' kappa with Gwet's AC1 and introduces Pearson correlation and ranking-concordance reporting. These extend statistical assessment beyond v1's practices. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty for the main model scores; additional language rows alone constitute additional results.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive results for three GUI agents, generator-source comparisons, correlations, and multilingual reliability. For example, Table 2 reports UI-TARS-7B-DPO FPR-ACC of 79.9 in English and 67.9 in Thai. All seven original models' benchmark scores are retained, and v1 Tables 3-4 match v2 Tables 4 and 6 numerically.

T1.justification: Eq. 3 substantively revises the mathematical definition of the memory key by excluding reasoning and answer context. The remaining residual-update, discrepancy, similarity, and normalized-intervention mathematics is equivalent apart from notation and presentation. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The benchmark, training-free intervention, and reported 6.5% average gain remain the central claims. v2 replaces the pipeline-focused contribution with comprehensive capability analysis, emphasizes controlled cross-lingual isolation, and adds an introduction-level claim that reasoning-chain results indicate representational improvement rather than a prompting artifact.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretation: low kappa is explained through the prevalence paradox and supplemented by high-AC1 reliability claims; generator comparisons are interpreted as evidence of stylistic neutrality; and RI/SI correlations are used to argue end-to-end validity. It also adds explanations for differential task gains and stronger mechanistic interpretations of reasoning-chain results.

D1.justification: v2 supplies model/language-specific layers and intervention strengths, ten-entry memories for basic dimensions, memory-selection criteria, and a validation-set tuning description. Appendices add annotator qualifications, language roles, tool assistance, compensation, adjudication, and refinement guidelines. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation without establishing that previously reported experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: Section 2 replaces the general LVLM-agent overview with a substantial cross-lingual representation-alignment discussion, adding representation-engineering and steering literature. Benchmark positioning expands to works including OSWorld, WebMMU, and X-WebAgentBench and foregrounds uncontrolled cross-language variation as a limitation of existing interactive benchmarks.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, method exposition, and result interpretations undergo extensive rewriting. Method subsections are reorganized, Appendix A is substantially restructured, and new ethics, acknowledgements, and LLM-use sections appear. Author and affiliation information also changes.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the overview and construction graphics, revises the hierarchical benchmark diagram, and replaces four task-specific sensitivity plots with two weighted-accuracy surfaces. It adds several analytical and documentation tables and three case-study figures. Earlier model results are split into an appendix table, while the method overview graphic is retained as Figure 15.

improvement.justification: Explicit intervention settings and memory details improve reproducibility, while additional GUI agents and generator-source controls improve diagnostic relevance. These gains are limited by weaknesses in the new validation: Table 17's Chinese rating counts imply observed agreement of approximately 0.9029, versus 0.9055 in Table 18. Moreover, correlating RI/SI with FPR-ACC, which already includes those components, provides limited support for the stronger end-to-end validity claim.
